sentences.text: Ela's grandmother explained it on the walk home in about four sentences.

It had three years of data — 2023, 2024, 2025 — from the national monitoring programme, which is a real programme run by serious people, and in those three years there had been no nest in the affected zone.
That is what the survey found and that is what the survey said.
The old woman had not nested in the affected zone since 2019.

She had nested there in 2019, and 2016, and 2015, and 2011, and in a great many years before that, and she moves up and down about two hundred metres of that beach in a way that nobody has ever charted because nobody has ever been paid to chart it.
"So why didn't anyone say?" Her grandmother walked for a while.
*We remember?* That woman had papers, Ela.
She had three years of counts done by people with clipboards.
If eleven of us stand up in a hall and say we recall a turtle being further along in about 2015, what is she supposed to do with that?
She'd be polite and she'd write it down and it would go nowhere, and she'd be right, because we would be eleven people remembering." Ela said that they would not be wrong.
Those are not opposites." Ela has thought about that sentence more than about anything else anybody said to her that year.
She said, on the road up from the school, that there had to be a way of turning one into the other.

Her grandmother said that there was, and that it was called evidence, and that the reason a town full of people who had watched a beach for sixty years had none of it was that not one of them had ever written anything down.
